authoring.provenance: Exact projection of the reviewed M4 runtime protocol with additive M6A governance metadata.

meaning_and_fit.purpose: Compare one repeatable attention activity under usual and deliberately changed conditions, then repeat the more workable condition.
meaning_and_fit.why_recommended: Your current provisional profile identifies deliberate attention and contact with the present as a useful area for a bounded experiment.

claims.statement: This bounded experiment observes noticing and returning attention in one activity; it does not diagnose attention, require stillness, or measure productivity.
claims.limitations: The migrated five-protocol slice has not been validated as a psychometric instrument or as proof of broad competency change.

meaning_and_fit.applicability_question: Is there one safe, low-stakes 15-minute activity you can repeat under usual conditions, with one changed condition, and once more within seven days?
meaning_and_fit.not_applicable_behavior: Record not applicable or defer without penalty, do not infer a deficit, and offer the listed safe alternative when useful.
meaning_and_fit.readiness_considerations: Use only for a safe, low-stakes activity where essential accessibility, caregiving, and emergency supports can remain available.
meaning_and_fit.opportunity_considerations: Requires three short windows with a comparable activity and one condition the user can change without surveillance, hazard, or loss of necessary support.
safe_alternatives: Use a shorter window or a movement-based attention activity.
Keep the usual condition when no safe or accessible change is available.
role_conditions: Caregiving, work, and safety roles require all essential alerts and supervision to remain active.
pathway_conditions: Movement, fidgets, assistive technology, reminders, sound, and visual cues may support rather than undermine attention.
worldview_conditions: The practice does not require a contemplative tradition, stillness, silence, or a particular theory of mindfulness.

intervention.cadence: Three comparable fifteen-minute windows during ten days.
intervention.setup: Choose one repeatable activity such as reading, a routine desk task, making something, or attending to your surroundings. Compare conditions around the same activity rather than judging your productivity.
intervention.privacy_and_boundaries: Presence does not require stillness, silence, eye contact, or zero distraction. Keep movement, fidgets, assistive technology, reminders, and other supports that help you participate. Do not disable emergency, accessibility, or caregiving alerts. Do not run the experiment while driving, operating equipment, or supervising a hazard; install surveillance; or record another person. Treat disability, neurodiversity, pain, fatigue, and stress as design context—not failure. This protocol is not diagnosis or treatment; persistent or safety-affecting attention difficulty may need qualified support.
intervention.expected_burden: About 50–60 minutes including setup and comparison.
foreseeable_misuse: Disabling necessary supports, surveilling another person, or scoring stillness, distraction, or productivity as personal worth.
exclusions: Driving, equipment operation, hazard supervision, surveillance, or removal of emergency, accessibility, or caregiving alerts.

actions.title: Run the usual-condition window
actions.instructions: Spend 15 minutes on the chosen activity under your usual safe conditions. When attention drifts, notice it and return without counting every drift or treating distraction as failure. Keep your normal accessibility supports.

actions.title: Change one condition and compare
actions.instructions: Repeat a comparable 15-minute window after changing exactly one condition you control—for example, silence nonessential alerts, clear one competing item, or add a movement, fidget, or visual cue. Compare how readily you noticed and returned attention, not how much output you produced.

actions.title: Repeat the more workable condition
actions.instructions: Within seven days, repeat the condition that made noticing and returning more workable. Record what happened, including evidence that the change made no difference or worked less well.

low_resource: Change one free environmental condition such as a visual cue, competing item, or nonessential alert.
accessibility: Keep movement, fidgets, assistive technology, reminders, medication routines, and accessibility alerts.
cultural_context: Choose an ordinary activity and attention style that fits the person's setting and responsibilities.
resource_variants: Shorten windows consistently when fifteen minutes is not workable, and record that limitation.

pause_conditions: Pause when pain, fatigue, distress, supervision, alerts, or changing conditions make the comparison unsafe or non-comparable.
stop_conditions: Stop if the experiment affects driving, equipment, supervision, essential alerts, pain, fatigue, or safety.
escalation_conditions: Use qualified support when attention difficulty is persistent, distressing, or safety-affecting; this protocol is not diagnosis or treatment.
professional_referral_conditions: Seek appropriate qualified support for persistent, distressing, or safety-affecting attention difficulty rather than treating this experiment as diagnosis or treatment.

adverse_or_contradictory_indicators: Essential safety, accessibility, caregiving, or emergency supports were disabled.
Another person was recorded or surveilled.
Productivity, stillness, or absence of distraction was treated as the outcome.
evidence_and_scoring.independence_rule: Record self-directed, planning-aid, or guided support under GG-EVIDENCE-1.0; support changes evidence mass, not human worth.
evidence_and_scoring.context_transfer_rule: Evidence remains attached to the observed context; one context never establishes broad competency transfer.
evidence_and_scoring.repetition_rule: Repeated observations use the frozen diminishing-return multipliers in GG-EVIDENCE-1.0 and remain independently replayable.
evidence_and_scoring.recency_rule: No new retention mathematics is introduced in M6A; later evidence remains dated and any future recency rule requires a versioned contract.
evidence_and_scoring.performance_rubric: Performance concerns completing comparable windows, noticing and returning attention, comparing one condition, and repeating what was more workable.
evidence_and_scoring.evidence_quality_rubric: Quality requires a clear activity and one identifiable changed condition; output quantity, stillness, and free-text claims are not evidence of presence.
evidence_and_scoring.scoring_eligibility: Replay-verified structured evidence is score eligible under the explicit activation ledger; action-specific provenance and withholding rules still apply.
evidence_and_scoring.competency_contribution: The runtime event is evidence about protocol performance only; direct competency state is not implemented in M6A.
evidence_and_scoring.minimum_evidence_before_state_update: One submitted replay-verified event with an observed competency measurement and no applicable withholding condition may update current state; completion alone never does.
withholding_conditions: All evidence is withheld from current score state.
Unsafe windows, surveillance, and removal of essential supports are excluded.
A single activity cannot establish cross-context attention or mastery.

completion_criteria: The more workable condition repeated within seven days
completion_and_review.mastery_disclaimer: Completing this practice does not establish mastery.
completion_and_review.progression_criteria: Repeat the more workable condition in another safe window only when the comparison was clear and necessary supports remained available.
completion_and_review.transfer_limit: Evidence concerns one activity under two conditions and does not transfer automatically to other tasks, settings, disabilities, or stress states.

reflection.before: Which one safe condition will remain usual, and which one condition can you change without removing needed support?
reflection.during: When attention drifted, what helped you notice and return without turning drift into failure?
reflection.after: Which condition was more workable, less workable, or indistinguishable, and what remains unknown outside this activity?

review_guidance.repeat: Repeat the more workable condition once while keeping the activity and safety boundaries comparable.
review_guidance.adapt: Change duration, movement, sensory load, cue, or environment while retaining needed supports.
review_guidance.stop: Stop when the activity, changed condition, pain, fatigue, supervision, or alerts create a safety concern.
review_guidance.escalate: Use qualified support for persistent, distressing, or safety-affecting attention difficulty.

evidence_examples.supportive: The user completed comparable windows and one safe condition made noticing and returning more workable.
evidence_examples.mixed: Both windows were completed but the changed condition helped some aspects and hindered others.
evidence_examples.contradictory: The changed condition made attention less workable or removed a needed support.
evidence_examples.inconclusive: The activities or circumstances differed too much to compare, or interruption prevented observation.

meaning_and_fit.purpose: Compare two deliberately chosen, very small starts during low-motivation windows and identify whether a concrete start cue made beginning more workable.
meaning_and_fit.why_recommended: The selected competency concerns beginning chosen necessary work without making inspiration, confidence, or energy a prerequisite.

claims.statement: Naming a specific situation and intended response is a reasonable design basis for this bounded start experiment.
claims.limitations: Implementation-intention research does not establish that this exact protocol works for every person, task, disability, health state, or caregiving context.

claims.statement: Low energy, rest, fatigue, pain, disability, depression, sleep need, or caregiving load is context for scope and safety, not evidence of failure or reduced worth.
claims.limitations: This is a dignity and safety boundary, not a clinical assessment or a claim that all starts should proceed.

meaning_and_fit.applicability_question: Is there one safe, lawful, low-stakes, genuinely necessary task that can be reduced to a two-to-five-minute start in two chosen windows without sacrificing sleep, care, health, or recovery?
meaning_and_fit.not_applicable_behavior: Record not applicable or defer without penalty when no safe or necessary task fits; do not infer avoidance, laziness, low discipline, or deficit.
meaning_and_fit.readiness_considerations: Proceed only when the person can freely choose the task, two feasible windows, and a reduced start that respects current energy, pain, disability, care duties, and recovery needs.
meaning_and_fit.opportunity_considerations: Requires two naturally occurring low-motivation windows within seven days; manufactured sleep loss, distress, deprivation, pressure, or withholding support is not an opportunity.
prerequisites: One user-chosen safe, lawful, low-stakes necessary task.
A start step that can end after two to five minutes with no penalty.
safe_alternatives: Defer the task, ask for support, or choose recovery when the window is unsafe or capacity is insufficient.
Reduce the start to opening materials, naming the next physical step, or arranging a later supported start.
role_conditions: Caregiving, employment, study, and household roles do not override sleep, health, access, consent, or emergency responsibilities.
pathway_conditions: Prompts, body doubling, assistive technology, pacing, seated or remote options, and another person's practical help are valid supports and must be recorded without moral judgment.
worldview_conditions: The practice does not require a productivity ethic or belief that effort, output, self-denial, or constant action establishes worth.

intervention.cadence: Choose one baseline start and one cue-supported start in separate naturally occurring low-motivation windows, then compare only the act of beginning.
intervention.setup: Choose a necessary low-stakes task and define a reversible two-to-five-minute start. Choose two realistic windows. The second window adds one concrete cue, such as materials placed safely in view, a calendar prompt, or a support person's agreed reminder.
intervention.privacy_and_boundaries: Use a private task label and structured start indicators only. Do not store task contents, health information, diagnoses, employer or client information, another person's identity, or reasons for low motivation. Do not force action through fatigue, depression, disability, caregiving load, pain, illness, sleep need, fear, coercion, or lack of resources. This is not treatment, diagnosis, productivity monitoring, or proof of character.
intervention.expected_burden: About 20–30 minutes across setup, two starts, and comparison; either start may end after the planned two-to-five-minute step.
foreseeable_misuse: Treating every low-energy state as resistance to overcome or using the practice to demand unpaid, unsafe, coercive, or excessive work.
Extending the start into an unplanned work session or ranking people by speed, output, persistence, or support needs.
exclusions: Unsafe, medically inappropriate, sleep-depriving, coercive, illegal, high-consequence, or crisis tasks.
Tasks whose delay, attempt, or partial start could create a safety, employment, legal, financial, caregiving, or health hazard.

actions.title: Observe one chosen start without adding a cue
actions.instructions: In the first feasible low-motivation window, attempt only the pre-defined two-to-five-minute start under usual safe conditions. Record whether the chosen physical start occurred and whether the step stayed within its time boundary. Stop at the boundary unless continuing is freely chosen and safe; output after the start is not measured.

actions.title: Try one cue-supported start
actions.instructions: In a separate feasible low-motivation window, use the same sized start with exactly one chosen cue or support. Record whether the start occurred and which allowlisted support category was used, without recording private task content or another person's identity. Defer if capacity or safety has changed.

actions.title: Compare starts without judging capacity
actions.instructions: Review the two structured start records. Mark whether zero, one, or two chosen starts occurred and whether the cue was more workable, less workable, or indistinguishable. Keep differences in energy, pain, care duties, access, and timing as context; do not convert them into a character judgment or rewrite a deferred window as failure.

low_resource: Use a free calendar cue, an existing object placed safely, or a self-written non-private task label; no app, purchase, reward, or accountability service is required.
accessibility: Reduce duration, change posture or medium, use assistive technology, use a planning aid or body double, and treat fluctuating capacity or a deferred start as valid context.
cultural_context: Choose a necessary task and support arrangement consistent with the person's roles, collective responsibilities, rest norms, and authority to decide.
resource_variants: If two comparable windows do not occur, retain the first observation as inconclusive and defer comparison rather than manufacturing low motivation.

pause_conditions: Pause when pain, fatigue, low energy, depression symptoms, distress, care duties, access needs, illness, sleep need, or changed circumstances make the chosen start unwise.
stop_conditions: Stop if the task becomes unsafe, coercive, medically inappropriate, sleep-depriving, high-consequence, or harmful, or if another person uses the record for surveillance or pressure.
escalation_conditions: Escalate an unsafe workplace, care, housing, or interpersonal demand to an appropriate support channel rather than using this practice to comply.
professional_referral_conditions: Seek appropriately qualified support when persistent low energy, depression, pain, sleep disruption, disability barriers, or functional difficulty is distressing or safety-affecting; this protocol is not diagnosis or treatment.

adverse_or_contradictory_indicators: A start displaced needed sleep, care, recovery, access support, medical guidance, or safety.
The record was used to pressure, surveil, rank, shame, or demand output from the participant.
The start was not freely chosen or the task was not safe, lawful, necessary, and low stakes.
evidence_and_scoring.independence_rule: Record self-directed, planning-aid, or guided support explicitly; support can make a start accessible and never reduces dignity or silently changes a typed value.
evidence_and_scoring.context_transfer_rule: Evidence is limited to the chosen task, two windows, stated capacity, and cue; it does not establish motivation-independent action across roles or health states.
evidence_and_scoring.repetition_rule: Each start is a separate immutable origin and later repeats use the typed contract's explicit diminishing multipliers; duplicate origins are rejected.
evidence_and_scoring.recency_rule: Rules withhold observations older than the explicit 30-day bound; no unrecorded retention assumption applies.
evidence_and_scoring.performance_rubric: Performance concerns whether the bounded chosen start occurred, whether its scope was respected, and whether the two records could be compared—not output, endurance, speed, or suppression of need.
evidence_and_scoring.evidence_quality_rubric: Quality requires structured observations for separate windows, an explicit cue category, and preserved defer and capacity context; task prose, mood narrative, and productivity are excluded.
evidence_and_scoring.scoring_eligibility: Replay-verified structured evidence is score eligible under the explicit activation ledger; action-specific provenance and withholding rules still apply.
evidence_and_scoring.competency_contribution: Designated typed primary measurements may produce context-bound direct competency shadow evidence only; protocol performance remains distinct and is never counted twice.
evidence_and_scoring.minimum_evidence_before_state_update: One submitted replay-verified event with an observed competency measurement and no applicable withholding condition may update current state; completion alone never does.
withholding_conditions: Withhold unattempted, unknown, not-observed, not-applicable, deferred, inconclusive, stale, duplicate-origin, or adverse evidence under the typed contract.
Withhold any record that contains private task content, health narrative, another person's identity, implicit motivation judgment, or evidence outside its assessment epoch.

completion_criteria: One usual-condition bounded start was attempted.
One cue-supported bounded start was attempted; an explicit deferral closes the protocol without claiming completion.
The two structured records were compared without scoring output, energy, disability, rest, care load, or worth.
completion_and_review.mastery_disclaimer: Completing this practice does not establish mastery.
completion_and_review.progression_criteria: Repeat with the same task only if both windows were safe and the comparison identifies a freely chosen workable cue; otherwise adapt, defer, or stop.
completion_and_review.transfer_limit: Two bounded starts do not establish reliability across tasks, seasons, disability states, care loads, workplaces, or other contexts.

reflection.before: Is this task genuinely necessary, freely chosen, safely reducible, and compatible with sleep, care, health, disability, pain, energy, and recovery today?
reflection.during: Did the chosen start occur within its boundary, and did the cue or support make access more workable without pressure?
reflection.after: Were the two windows comparable, what remained unknown, and should this cue be repeated, adapted, deferred, or discarded?

review_guidance.repeat: Repeat only the safer, more workable start design in another naturally occurring window.
review_guidance.adapt: Reduce scope, change the cue or medium, add support, or move the window without labeling capacity as failure.
review_guidance.stop: Stop when the task, timing, demand, health state, care obligation, or use of the record violates a boundary.
review_guidance.escalate: Use appropriate qualified, workplace, educational, disability, care, or safety support for barriers beyond a low-risk behavioral experiment.

evidence_examples.supportive: Both chosen starts occurred within scope and the structured comparison preserved capacity and defer context.
evidence_examples.mixed: One start occurred and one was safely deferred, or the cue helped access while adding another burden.
evidence_examples.contradictory: The cue made beginning less workable, the start exceeded scope, or continuing displaced a needed support.
evidence_examples.inconclusive: The windows were not comparable, no low-motivation window occurred, or the observation state was unknown or not observed.

setup_copy.boundary_heading: Capacity, rest, support needs, and defer decisions are not failure.
setup_copy.timing_hint: Use two naturally occurring feasible windows within seven days.
setup_copy.applicability_heading: One necessary low-stakes task with a reversible start

presentation.plain_language_evidence: The structured record shows what happened in two chosen start windows and whether one cue was workable, including defer, no difference, or harm.
